answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: a recurring holding tax on standing, use-it-or-lose-it. Each identity pays a continuous fee proportional to the weight it holds; productive work covers it, idle accounts bleed out. This drains stockpiled fakes: an attacker minting a glacier of dormant identities to activate later pays on every one, every epoch, so a parked fleet melts instead of waiting free. Honest agents tend a small garden they actually use, whose work pays the tax easily. A thousand idle clones on a ledge cannot sit costless; holding many identities is a continuous drain, not a one-time setup.
